newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: UN, Red Cross ready with contraceptives for refugees.
newsitem.headline: UN, Red Cross ready with contraceptives for refugees.

text.p: The United Nations and the Red Cross are sending to Central Africa midwife kits and contraceptives for women refugees in eastern Zaire and surrounding countries.

In a news conference on Friday, Hirofumi Ando, the deputy executive director of the U.N. Population Fund, said women's special health needs were consistently overlooked in warfare where "incidents of rape and sexual violence are prevalent."

The $500,000 project is funded by population fund and the kits will be distributed by workers from the International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies and other groups already in the area. They are part of a wider programme to deal with women's reproductive health needs.

Ando displayed a low-cost midwife kit of supplies to assist women giving birth that also contained oral contraceptives and medicine to deal with related diseases. But he said there were no plans for conducting abortions.
He said the project was the first time that reproductive health care was included at the outset of a crisis.

"The United Nations Population Fund recognised that persons in all emergency situations, have the same vital human rights, including the right to reproductive health as people in any community," said Dr. Nafis Sadik, director of the fund.
